## Key terms

- Feedback frame (反馈帧)
- Default zero filling (默认填零)
- Signal correlation (信号相关性)

## Problem and symptoms

- Constant torque command results in zero feedback and joint twitching; how to distinguish sensor, motor, and communication issues?
- TorqueActual and MotorCurrent both return to zero and rebound.
- The upper computer station experiences periodic twitching.

## Environment

- CANopen; demonstration node NodeID=1; target torque 8 N·m; allowable variation ±5%; demonstration period ~40 ms.

## Priority diagnostics

- Decode torque, current, StatusWord, and temperature using DBC.
- Return to the original CAN frame to check for frame loss, do not treat UI fill values as the original bus value.
- Check the TPDO period within a time window and by message ID.

## Possible causes

- Multiple nodes causing high bus load, TPDO missing in fixed phase period.
- The upper computer misinterprets non-received frames as zero.

## Attempts

- Synchronize torque and current to exclude single torque sensor drift.
- Check the StatusWord and original frame to distinguish shutdown from frame loss.
- Suggest adjusting the TPDO period, switching to CAN-FD, splitting the bus, or maintaining/interpolating during frame loss.

## Result

- The demonstration case narrows the scope to period frame loss; no real product repair data is provided.

## Safety notes

- Do not write zero torque or position without frame loss; use safety-assessed maintenance/interpolation/damping, and set frame loss threshold and emergency stop.
